subject.title: Clarify or preserve skill source provenance from CLI publish

question: Should skill-publish source flags create separately visible unverified publisher attribution, remain non-visible with explicit documentation, or be replaced by a server-verification workflow?
rationale: This defines a public CLI/API contract and determines whether user-controlled metadata appears near trusted supply-chain signals, so source inspection cannot safely infer the permanent policy.

options.title: Separate unverified attribution
options.body: Store and expose publisher-declared source under a distinct field and UI label that cannot be confused with verified provenance.

options.title: Document non-visible metadata
options.body: Preserve current behavior and explicitly state that these flags do not create provenance, a GitHub-backed skill, or a public source link.

options.title: Build verified CLI publishing
options.body: Verify repository access, commit and path identity, and uploaded-content equivalence before setting trusted provenance.

recommendation.title: Separate unverified attribution
recommendation.body: Store and expose publisher-declared source under a distinct field and UI label that cannot be confused with verified provenance.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged GitHub-backed source implementation is the strongest direct ownership signal for this provenance architecture.
